fixes.explanation: Wise sounds nice, but that's not what he's after. He says, “If You are willing, You can make me clean.” (Mark 1:40) The word he picks is clean, not wise. Nobody's asking for a bigger brain here, baker.
I get the guess, because it takes guts to drop to your knees and beg. But brave isn't what he asks for. He says, “If You are willing, You can make me clean.” (Mark 1:40) Clean is the word he picks.
That's it, baker. “If You are willing, You can make me clean.” (Mark 1:40) He says Jesus can make him clean, and the "if" is about whether Jesus is willing. I think that's a humble way to ask.

Close in spirit, but those aren't his words. He says, “If You are willing, You can make me clean.” (Mark 1:40) The "if" lands on Jesus being willing. The man does speak about himself, but what he asks is to be made clean, not a word about being worthy.

True! Mark says, “Moved with compassion, Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man.” (Mark 1:41) Compassion moves Him, and His hand reaches out. Then He tells the man He is willing. I think this is a tender moment.

It's actually true, friend. The text says, “Moved with compassion, Jesus reached out His hand and touched the man.” (Mark 1:41) Compassion moves Him, and He reaches out His hand. Then He tells the man He is willing.

Tell is the word. Jesus says, “See that you don’t tell anyone.” (Mark 1:44) That's a big ask when you've just been healed. It's like getting the best news of your life and being told to keep it out of the group chat.
Not visit, friend. The warning is, “See that you don’t tell anyone.” (Mark 1:44) Jesus does tell him to show himself to the priest, but the stern warning is about keeping quiet.

Scribes, huh? Solid guess, baker, but that's not who Jesus names. He says, “But go, show yourself to the priest…” (Mark 1:44) Priest is the word on the page, and I've stamped enough wrong guesses in my day to say there's no shame in it.

Ooh, so close to a good plan, but no. Mark says, “But the man went out and openly began to proclaim and spread the news.” (Mark 1:45) Jesus said not to tell anyone, and this man openly begins to proclaim and spread the news. That's the opposite of keeping it to himself.

Crowds sent away? I'd love to sell you that one, baker, but it's not in there. Mark says, “Consequently, Jesus could no longer enter a town in plain view…” (Mark 1:45) The change is about where He can go. And the verse ends with, “Yet people came to Him from every quarter.”
